To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the equity risk premium and the credit risk spread in a world with disasters are both positive and that they increase with the probability of disaster, the degree of leverage and the degree of correlation between output and the value of the risky assets.

(i) the riskless rate and equity risk premium are determined by the probability of default of the corporate sector, and (ii) the credit risk premium is determined by the probability and severity of default of the Government.

the credit risk spread is a function of leverage and the equity risk premium, that the latter is a function of the equity premium and the riskless rate (which are in turn functions of output volatility and the probability of disaster) and that the credit risk premium is a function of all of the above.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of disasters on the riskless rate and the equity premium.
the credit risk premium in a disaster-prone world.

the role played by the riskiness of the corporate sector in the presence of disasters, as well as with the role played, within the corporate sector, by the credit market in determining the equity premium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the credit risk premium in the Barro model is a function of the leverage ratio and the volatility of the output process, and that the leverage ratio is the main driver.
the model is consistent with the observed risk premia and that the data are consistent with the model.
the Barro (2008) model is consistent with the data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to generate the observed risk premia in the presence of leverage and extreme events.
the credit risk premium in the model is a combination of a riskless rate, a risk premium and a credit risk premium.

we have shown that a model of the riskless interest rate, equity risk premia, and corporate credit spreads that is consistent with the data can be obtained by assuming that the government never defaults, that the corporate sector defaults only in the most severe states of the world, that the probability of default is endogenous, and that the corporate sector has no leverage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the credit spread is an important determinant of the equity risk premia, and that the equity risk premium is a good proxy for the credit risk spread.
the credit risk spread, as well as the equity risk premium, can be explained by the presence of extreme states, even if these states are not associated with a Government default.
the credit risk premium is not a residual, but is a fundamental component of the equity risk spread, and should be taken into account in any model of the equity premium.
